overview: Cawsand is one of a pair of pretty villages, with Kingsand next door, on the Rame Peninsula in Cornwall’s ‘forgotten corner’, looking out over Plymouth Sound. The beach is a small mix of sand and shingle, with rock pools to explore, right below the village.

The villages are full of history, from repelling a Spanish raid in 1596 to Nelson reputedly staying here, and they’re surrounded by Mount Edgcumbe Country Park, so there are lovely walks right on the doorstep.

expect.title: The beach
expect.text: A small sand and shingle beach with a network of rock pools.

expect.title: The villages
expect.text: Narrow lanes, colourful cottages and two pubs, the Cross Keys and The Bay.

expect.title: Mount Edgcumbe
expect.text: The country park wraps around the villages, with woods and coastal paths to explore.

goodToKnow.label: Getting there
goodToKnow.text: There’s a bus service, and a seasonal ferry runs to and from Plymouth.

week.text: A gentle, sheltered beach day in the far south-east, as the beach faces east away from the prevailing winds. Combine it with a walk through Mount Edgcumbe or the big beaches of Whitsand Bay over the hill.

pairWith.why: a historic house and country park next door
a long sandy beach on Whitsand Bay
the twin village right next door

tips: Pack a bucket and net for the rock pools at low tide.
